lem-type-s-posterior-preliminary-contrac.claim:
Assume AC for the imported measure and Gaussian interfaces. Use Type-S priors and either cutoff of [[def-type-s-and-h-multiscale-density-priors]] with the compact multiresolution basis of [[lem-compact-wavelet-projection-kernel-and-commutator]], regular enough for the truth's Hölder approximation. Suppose $0<\rho_0\le f_0\le D_0$, $g_0=\log f_0\in C^\alpha$, and $\alpha>1/2$. In S1 take $\sigma_l=2^{-l(\alpha+1/2)}$ and any probability density whose logarithm is Lipschitz on all of $\mathbb R$. In S2 take Gaussian coefficients with $\sigma_l=2^{-l(r+1/2)}$ and $0<r<\alpha-1/4$.

Write $d=\dim V_{L_n}\asymp2^{L_n}$, $E_{L_n}=V_{L_n}\cap\{h:\int h=0\}$, $\theta=T-\int T$, $\theta_*=P_{L_n}g_0-\int g_0$, and $e_n=\sqrt{d/n}+d^{-\alpha}$. Under IID data of density $f_0$, the posterior distributions of $\|\theta-\theta_*\|_2/e_n$ are tight in probability. Equivalently, for every deterministic $b_n\to\infty$,
$$\Pi(\|\theta-\theta_*\|_2>b_ne_n\mid X^n)\to0$$
in $P_0^n$-probability. The normalizer defining the posterior is positive and finite $P_0^n$-almost surely. The quotient prior has a positive continuous Lebesgue density $q_L$ on $E_L$. In S1 it obeys
$$|\log q_L(\theta+u)-\log q_L(\theta)|\le B_L\|u\|_2,\qquad B_L^2\le C\sum_{l\le L}2^l\sigma_l^{-2},$$
and a shift in a single high wavelet coordinate obeys the sharper bound $C|u_{lk}|/\sigma_l$. The low scaling block has a fixed finite collection of analogous weighted bounds. In S2 the quotient prior is centered Gaussian, with precision $Q_L$ diagonal on high wavelets with entries $\sigma_l^{-2}$ and a fixed positive definite low scaling block. Its log-density increment is $-\langle Q_L\theta,u\rangle-\langle Q_Lu,u\rangle/2$.

citations.quote:
Assume AC for the imported measure and Gaussian interfaces. Use Type-S priors and either cutoff of [[def-type-s-and-h-multiscale-density-priors]] with the compact multiresolution basis of [[lem-compact-wavelet-projection-kernel-and-commutator]], regular enough for the truth's Hölder approximation. Suppose $0<\rho_0\le f_0\le D_0$, $g_0=\log f_0\in C^\alpha$, and $\alpha>1/2$. In S1 take $\sigma_l=2^{-l(\alpha+1/2)}$ and any probability density whose logarithm is Lipschitz on all of $\mathbb R$. In S2 take Gaussian coefficients with $\sigma_l=2^{-l(r+1/2)}$ and $0<r<\alpha-1/4$.

Write $d=\dim V_{L_n}\asymp2^{L_n}$, $E_{L_n}=V_{L_n}\cap\{h:\int h=0\}$, $\theta=T-\int T$, $\theta_*=P_{L_n}g_0-\int g_0$, and $e_n=\sqrt{d/n}+d^{-\alpha}$. Under IID data of density $f_0$, the posterior distributions of $\|\theta-\theta_*\|_2/e_n$ are tight in probability. Equivalently, for every deterministic $b_n\to\infty$,
$$\Pi(\|\theta-\theta_*\|_2>b_ne_n\mid X^n)\to0$$
in $P_0^n$-probability. The normalizer defining the posterior is positive and finite $P_0^n$-almost surely. The quotient prior has a positive continuous Lebesgue density $q_L$ on $E_L$. In S1 it obeys
$$|\log q_L(\theta+u)-\log q_L(\theta)|\le B_L\|u\|_2,\qquad B_L^2\le C\sum_{l\le L}2^l\sigma_l^{-2},$$
and a shift in a single high wavelet coordinate obeys the sharper bound $C|u_{lk}|/\sigma_l$. The low scaling block has a fixed finite collection of analogous weighted bounds. In S2 the quotient prior is centered Gaussian, with precision $Q_L$ diagonal on high wavelets with entries $\sigma_l^{-2}$ and a fixed positive definite low scaling block. Its log-density increment is $-\langle Q_L\theta,u\rangle-\langle Q_Lu,u\rangle/2$.

Let $V_L$ be the span of wavelets through level $L$ in a compactly supported orthonormal multiresolution basis on $[0,1]$, either boundary corrected or periodized. Assume constants belong to $V_L$, its dimension $d_L\asymp2^L$, and its orthonormal scaling functions $\phi_{Lk}$ have supremum norm at most $C2^{L/2}$, support diameter at most $C2^{-L}$, and uniformly bounded overlap. Periodized supports and distances are interpreted on the circle. Assume also $\sum_k|\psi_{lk}(x)|\le C2^{l/2}$ and $\|\psi_{lk}\|_1\le C2^{-l/2}$. Let $P_L$ denote the orthogonal projection onto $V_L$.

Then $P_L$ has a kernel $K_L$ satisfying $\sup_x\int|K_L(x,y)|dy\le C'$ and $K_L(x,y)=0$ when $\operatorname{dist}(x,y)>C'2^{-L}$. If $a$ is $\beta$-Hölder for $0<\beta\le1$, then
$$\|P_L(ah)-ah\|_\infty\le C'\|a\|_{C^\beta}2^{-\beta L}\|h\|_\infty,\qquad h\in V_L.$$
For the composition assertion, assume additionally an integer $m>\alpha$ such that $\|\psi_{lk}^{(q)}\|_\infty\le C_q2^{l(q+1/2)}$ for $0\le q\le m$, bounded overlap also for their derivatives, and vanishing moments through degree $m-1$ for the detail wavelets, including boundary wavelets; the finite low scaling functions are $C^m$. These are the usual sufficiently regular compact wavelet hypotheses. If a bounded function $g$ has coefficients bounded by $C_g2^{-l(\alpha+1/2)}$, with $\alpha>0$, and its wavelet expansion represents $g$ in $L^2$, then $\|g-P_Lg\|_\infty\le C''C_g2^{-\alpha L}$, up to equality of the continuous representatives. Under these additional derivative and cancellation hypotheses, $e^g$ also has coefficients bounded by $C_g^\prime2^{-l(\alpha+1/2)}$, including integer $\alpha$, and $g,e^g$ are $\beta$-Hölder for every $0<\beta<\min(\alpha,1)$. Moreover $\|h\|_\infty\le C''\sqrt{d_L}\|h\|_2$ for $h\in V_L$.

Assume AC. Let $P_0$ have density $0\le f_0\le D<\infty$ on $[0,1]$, and let $(\psi_{lk})$ be an orthonormal wavelet system with at most $C2^l$ coordinates per level, including finitely many coarsest scaling coordinates. The Haar system is allowed. For every admissible $w$, there exists a Borel centered Gaussian random element $G_{P_0}$ of $M_0(w)$ with coefficient covariance
$$K((l,k),(l',k'))=P_0[(\psi_{lk}-P_0\psi_{lk})(\psi_{l'k'}-P_0\psi_{l'k'})].$$
Its Borel law is uniquely determined by these finite-coordinate Gaussian laws.

Let $Q_n$ be data-indexed probability measures on $M_0(w)$ and let $G$ be a fixed probability measure on this space. For the projections $P_J$ of [[lem-m0w-separable-and-projection-tails]], suppose that for every fixed $J$,
$$\beta_{BL}(Q_n\circ P_J^{-1},G\circ P_J^{-1})\to0$$
in probability, and that for every $\varepsilon,\eta>0$,
$$\lim_{J\to\infty}\limsup_{n\to\infty}P\left\{Q_n(\|x-P_Jx\|_{M(w)}>\varepsilon)>\eta\right\}=0.$$
Then $\beta_{BL}(Q_n,G)\to0$ in probability.

Let $Z_1,\ldots,Z_m$ be independent, integrable, centered real random variables on a probability space, with $|Z_i|\le b$ almost surely for a finite $b>0$. Put $S_m=\sum_{i=1}^mZ_i$ and $V=\sum_{i=1}^m\mathbb E[Z_i^2]$. For every $t>0$, if $V>0$ then
$$\mathbb P(S_m\ge t)\le\exp\!\left(-\frac{t^2}{2(V+bt/3)}\right),\qquad \mathbb P(S_m\le-t)\le\exp\!\left(-\frac{t^2}{2(V+bt/3)}\right).$$
If $V=0$, then $S_m=0$ almost surely.
Assume AC. A family $\mathcal A$ of Borel probabilities on a Polish space S is tight if and only if it is relatively sequentially compact for weak convergence.

Assume AC. Two Borel probability laws on $\mathbb R$ with equal characteristic functions are equal. In particular a real random variable has a real-valued characteristic function if and only if its law is symmetric under $x\mapsto-x$.

Assume AC. Let $d\ge1$ be a finite integer and $p_\theta(x)=\theta\cdot x$ for $\theta\in\mathbb R^d$. Borel probability laws on $\mathbb R^d$ are determined by all the laws $(p_\theta)_*\mu$. Moreover, if $(p_\theta)_*\mu_n\Rightarrow(p_\theta)_*\mu$ for every $\theta$ and a specified Borel probability law $\mu$, then $\mu_n\Rightarrow\mu$. If dimension zero is admitted, interpret $\mathbb R^0$ as the singleton empty tuple; both conclusions then hold as well.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $(S,d)$ be a Polish space, and let $\mu_n,\mu$ be Borel probability measures on $S$. Define

$$\beta_{BL}(\nu,\rho):=\sup\left\{\left|\int g\,d\nu-\int g\,d\rho\right|:g:S\to\mathbb R,\ \|g\|_\infty\le1,\ \operatorname{Lip}_d(g)\le1\right\},$$

where $\operatorname{Lip}_d(g):=\sup_{x\ne y}|g(x)-g(y)|/d(x,y)$, with value $0$ when $S$ has at most one point. Then

$$\mu_n\Rightarrow\mu\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\beta_{BL}(\mu_n,\mu)\longrightarrow0,$$

where $\Rightarrow$ is weak convergence of Borel probabilities ([[def-weak-convergence-of-borel-probability-measures]]). The implication from bounded-Lipschitz convergence to weak convergence is choice-free; the reverse implication below uses AC through Prokhorov's theorem.

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be an arbitrary measure space. All functions below have domain $X$. Let $f$ and $(f_n)$ be measurable complex-valued functions such that
$f_n\to f$ almost everywhere and $|f_n|\le g$ almost everywhere for a single
nonnegative measurable function $g$ with $\int g\,d\mu<+\infty$. Then
$f\in L^1(\mu)$,
$$\int|f_n-f|\,d\mu\longrightarrow0,$$
and hence
$$\int f_n\,d\mu\longrightarrow\int f\,d\mu.$$

If $X:\Omega\to[0,+\infty]$ is a nonnegative random variable on a probability
space and $a>0$, then
$$\mathbb P(X\ge a)\le\frac{\mathbb E[X]}{a}.$$

derivations.claim: Choose a deterministic $b_n\to\infty$ sufficiently slowly that $b_n\sqrt d e_n\to0$ and $b_ne_nd^{2r+1}/\sqrt n\to0$ in the Gaussian case. Such a choice exists: the first unmultiplied expression tends to zero because $\alpha>1/2$, and the second is bounded by a logarithmic factor times $d^{2r-2\alpha+1/2}\to0$. Set $D_n=\{\|\theta-\theta_*\|_2\le b_ne_n\}$ in the quotient by constants used in [F1]. Then $\Pi(D_n\mid X^n)\to1$ in probability. On $D_n$, $\|\theta-\theta_*\|_\infty\le Cb_n\sqrt d e_n=o(1)$; hence $\|f-f_0\|_\infty=o(1)$ uniformly, and the densities are bounded above and away from zero. Write $\Pi_D$ for the posterior conditioned on $D_n$.

For $\gamma=\psi_{lk}$, $l\le L_n$, define $f_s=fe^{-s\gamma/\sqrt n}/P_fe^{-s\gamma/\sqrt n}$. For $|s|\le\sqrt{\lambda_l}$, Taylor expansion of the log moment generating function gives $s\sqrt n(P_f-P_n)\gamma=\ell_n(f_s)-\ell_n(f)+(s^2/2)\operatorname{Var}_f\gamma+R$, where $|R|\le C|s|^3\|\gamma\|_\infty/\sqrt n$. To justify the uniform remainder, differentiate $a\mapsto\log P_fe^{a\gamma}$ three times; its third derivative is the third centered moment under the tilted density, bounded by $C\|\gamma\|_\infty P_f\gamma^2$ when $|a|\|\gamma\|_\infty=o(1)$. On $D_n$, $P_f\gamma^2\le C$ by orthonormality and the density bound, while $\sqrt{L_n}2^{L_n/2}/\sqrt n\to0$. Thus $|R|\le Cs^2$ and $\operatorname{Var}_f\gamma\le C$. Here $\ell_n$ is the sum log likelihood.

The map $f\mapsto f_s$ is the quotient-coordinate translation $\theta\mapsto\theta-s(\gamma-\int\gamma)/\sqrt n$. On high wavelets it shifts one coordinate; low scaling directions involve only a fixed finite-dimensional block. In S1 the absolute log prior density ratio is at most $C|s|/(\sqrt n\sigma_l)\le C|s|$, since $2^{L_n(\alpha+1/2)}\le\sqrt n$. In S2 it is at most $C[|s|(|g_{0,lk}|+b_ne_n)/(\sqrt n\sigma_l^2)+s^2/(n\sigma_l^2)]$, with a bounded fixed low-block version. Uniformly in high $l\le L_n$, its coefficients are bounded: $|g_{0,lk}|\le C2^{-l(\alpha+1/2)}$, $b_ne_nd^{2r+1}/\sqrt n=o(1)$, and $d^{2r+1}/n=o(1)$. Changing variables in the numerator likelihood integral and discarding its transformed $D_n$ indicator therefore bounds that integral by $e^{C|s|+Cs^2}$ times the full posterior normalizer. Step 1.2 yields $E_{\Pi_D}e^{s\sqrt n(P_f-P_n)\psi_{lk}}\le Ce^{Cs^2+C|s|}/\Pi(D_n\mid X^n)$. No translation invariance of $D_n$ is used.

Put $Z_{lk}=\sqrt n\langle f-P_n,\psi_{lk}\rangle$ for $l\le L_n$ and $p_n=\Pi(D_n\mid X^n)$. Exponential Markov with $s=\pm\sqrt{\lambda_l}$ gives $\Pi_D\{|Z_{lk}|>u\sqrt{\lambda_l}\}\le Cp_n^{-1}e^{-\lambda_l(u-C)}$. Union over the at most $C2^l$ locations shows $E_{\Pi_D}\max_k|Z_{lk}|\le Cp_n^{-1}\sqrt{\lambda_l}$. Union also over levels and integrate in $u$ above a sufficiently large constant to obtain $E_{\Pi_D}\sup_{l\le L_n,k}|Z_{lk}|/\sqrt{\lambda_l}\le C/p_n$: the relevant integral is bounded by $Cp_n^{-1}\sum_{l\ge1}2^l\int_M^\infty e^{-l(u-C)}du$, plus a finite low-level term. Also the wavelet level bound and a geometric sum give $E_{\Pi_D}\|P_{L_n}(f-P_n)\|_\infty\le Cp_n^{-1}\sqrt{d\lambda_{L_n}/n}$.

Each empirical wavelet coordinate has variance at most $D_0/n$ and summands bounded by $C2^{l/2}$. Bernstein [F5] gives $\Pr\{|(P_n-P_0)\psi_{lk}|>C[\sqrt{t/n}+2^{l/2}t/n]\}\le2e^{-t}$. Choose $t=C'(l+1)+u$, union over $k$, and integrate over $u\ge0$ to get $E\max_k|(P_n-P_0)\psi_{lk}|\le C[\sqrt{\lambda_l/n}+2^{l/2}\lambda_l/n]$. Summing against $2^{l/2}$ yields $\|P_{L_n}(P_n-P_0)\|_\infty=O_P(\sqrt{d\lambda_{L_n}/n}+d\lambda_{L_n}/n)=O_P(\sqrt{d\lambda_{L_n}/n})$, since $d\lambda_{L_n}/n\to0$. Moreover $\|P_{L_n}f_0-f_0\|_\infty\le Cd^{-\alpha}\le C\sqrt{d\lambda_{L_n}/n}$ for both cutoffs. Consequently the posterior projected density error is tight at rate $a_n=\sqrt{d\lambda_{L_n}/n}$.

This projected rate controls the full supremum error. Put $h=\theta-\theta_*$, $f_*=e^{\theta_*}/\int e^{\theta_*}$, and $v=h-P_{f_*}h\in V_{L_n}$. Since $\int h=0$, $\|h\|_\infty\le2\|v\|_\infty$. Normalized exponential expansion gives $f-f_*=f_*v+R$ with $\|R\|_\infty\le C\|h\|_\infty^2$ on $D_n$. Also $\|f_*-f_0\|_\infty\le Cd^{-\alpha}$. For any fixed $0<\beta<\min(\alpha,1)$, $f_0$ is $\beta$-Hölder, so [F2] gives $\|P_{L_n}(f_0v)-f_0v\|_\infty\le Cd^{-\beta}\|v\|_\infty$. The lower bound $f_0\ge\rho_0$ and uniform boundedness of $P_{L_n}$ imply $c\|h\|_\infty\le\|P_{L_n}(f-f_0)\|_\infty+C d^{-\beta}\|h\|_\infty+C\|h\|_\infty^2+Cd^{-\alpha}$. Step 1.1 makes the two terms proportional to $\|h\|_\infty$ absorbable. It follows that $\|f-f_0\|_\infty\le C[\|P_{L_n}(f-f_0)\|_\infty+d^{-\alpha}]$ uniformly on $D_n$. Thus the full posterior supremum error is tight at rate $a_n$.

Fix a finite linear combination $\gamma$ of wavelets and a fixed real $s$. Repeat step 1.2 with this bounded $\gamma$. Its remainder is now $o(1)$, and $\operatorname{Var}_f\gamma\to\operatorname{Var}_0\gamma$ uniformly on $D_n$. The prior translation involves finitely many fixed coordinates, and its density ratio tends to one uniformly on $D_n$: use the global S1 log-Lipschitz bound or the fixed Gaussian precision block and bounded quotient coordinates in S2. Let $A_s$ be the translated image of $D_n$. For large $n$, $A_s$ contains $D_n^-:=\{\|\theta-\theta_*\|_2\le b_ne_n/2\}$ because the translation has norm $O(n^{-1/2})=o(b_ne_n)$. Both $\Pi(D_n^-\mid X^n)$ and $\Pi(D_n\mid X^n)$ tend to one by [F1]. Bounding the translated integral above by the full normalizer and below by its integral on $D_n^-$ therefore gives $E_{\Pi_D}e^{s\sqrt n(P_f-P_n)\gamma}\to e^{s^2\operatorname{Var}_0(\gamma)/2}$ in probability.

Here is the needed finite-dimensional Laplace continuity argument. Along any subsequence, extract a further subsequence on which the preceding transform convergences hold almost surely for every rational $s$ and every rational vector of finite-coordinate coefficients, using countability and convergence in probability. The transforms at the positive and negative coordinate unit vectors give tightness of these deterministic finite-dimensional laws by exponential Markov and a finite union bound. [F6] gives a weakly convergent further subsequence. For a fixed rational direction and rational $s$, its exponential is uniformly integrable: its second moment is bounded by the transform at $2s$, and Cauchy–Schwarz and Markov bound the expectation above any large cutoff. Truncation thus passes its transform to the weak limit. In each coordinate direction and then any rational linear direction, the limit has finite exponential moments of every rational order, and hence of every real order by bounding $e^{t|x|}$ by $e^{q x}+e^{-q x}$ for rational $q>|t|$. Its moment generating function is analytic: on every bounded complex disk its power series can be integrated term by term under $e^{q|x|}$. Equality with the Gaussian transform on the rationals therefore gives equality of all moments by the real power series at zero. Integrating the characteristic-function power series under the same exponential bound gives the Gaussian characteristic function. [F6] identifies every rational linear projection with the corresponding centered normal. Continuity of characteristic functions in their vector argument extends the identification to real vectors; [F6] then identifies the finite-dimensional law with the Gaussian projection of [F3]. Every weakly convergent further subsequence has that limit, so tightness implies weak convergence of the full deterministic subsequence, and [F7] gives bounded-Lipschitz convergence. The initial subsequence argument proves convergence in probability of the original random projected laws.

For the coefficients through $L_n$, step 2.1 and Markov give posterior tightness of $\sup_{l\le L_n,k}|Z_{lk}|/\sqrt{\lambda_l}$. Therefore for $J<L_n$, the $M(w)$ norm of the part with $J<l\le L_n$ is at most this variable times $\sup_{l>J}\sqrt{\lambda_l}/w_l$, which tends to zero as $J\to\infty$ by admissibility. This proves the required uniform projected posterior tail bound.

Choose $M_n\to\infty$ so slowly that $M_n\sqrt{\lambda_{L_n}}/w_{L_n}\to0$. Step 2.3 makes the posterior probability of $\|f-f_0\|_\infty>M_na_n$ tend to zero. On its complement, the $L^1$ wavelet bound and monotonicity of $w$ give $\sqrt n\|P_{>L_n}(f-f_0)\|_{M(w)}\le C\sqrt n2^{-L_n/2}w_{L_n}^{-1}M_na_n\le CM_n\sqrt{\lambda_{L_n}}/w_{L_n}\to0$. The truth coefficients satisfy $\sqrt n\|P_{>L_n}f_0\|_{M(w)}\le C\sqrt n d^{-\alpha-1/2}/w_{L_n}\le C\sqrt{\lambda_{L_n}}/w_{L_n}\to0$ for either cutoff. Hence the entire density tail above $L_n$ is negligible in posterior probability.

Each density is a finite exponential of bounded continuous functions, hence belongs to $L^2$; its coefficients, and those of $P_n(L_n)$, belong to $M_0(w)$. Removing $D_n$ changes posterior integrals of functions bounded by one by at most $2[1-\Pi(D_n\mid X^n)]=o_P(1)$. Step 3.2 supplies fixed finite-projection convergence to [F3], and steps 4.1–4.2 supply the posterior-tail condition. Apply [F4] to conclude the asserted bounded-Lipschitz convergence in $M_0(w)$.

boundaries.reason: Statement: the IID density model is nonempty and each finite projection retains the fixed low scaling space.

boundaries.evidence: Proof 3.1–3.2: gamma=0 and zero-variance constant directions have transform one and Dirac Gaussian limit; no variance division occurs.
Proof 3.2: the Laplace continuity argument covers a single scalar coordinate, and the fixed low-level cases use lambda_l=max(l,1) in 1.2–2.2.
Proof 3.2: singular finite bridge covariance is allowed because linear projections of variance zero are Dirac; F3 supplies the joint Borel Gaussian law.
Statement retains S1 alpha>1 and S2 alpha>1/2 with strict r<alpha-1/4. The integer-alpha exp composition is supplied by F2. Both cutoffs and interval boundary wavelets are covered.
Statement explicitly assumes full AC, used in F3 Gaussian construction and F6 Prokhorov/characteristic uniqueness; step 3.2 uses countable diagonal subsequences within that scope.

boundaries.reason: Statement asserts a sufficient weak-BvM theorem, not a necessary-and-sufficient criterion.
Statement asserts no converse for failed prior or truth hypotheses.

thm-type-s-density-weak-bvm-on-m0w.claim:
Assume AC. Let $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ be IID on $[0,1]$ with density $0<\rho_0\le f_0\le D_0<\infty$, and suppose $g_0=\log f_0\in C^\alpha$. Use a sufficiently regular compactly supported boundary corrected orthonormal multiresolution wavelet basis satisfying [[lem-compact-wavelet-projection-kernel-and-commutator]], with regularity greater than $\alpha$, and let $V_L$ contain exactly its wavelet levels through $L$, including the fixed low scaling space and constants. Its regularity and vanishing moments satisfy the composition hypotheses in that lemma for some integer $m>\alpha$. Let $L_n$ be either of the two cutoff sequences in [[def-type-s-and-h-multiscale-density-priors]], fixed consistently for all $n$.

In Type-S1 take $\alpha>1$, $\sigma_l=2^{-l(\alpha+1/2)}$, and any coefficient probability density with globally Lipschitz logarithm. def-multiscale-coefficient-space-m0w.claim:
Use the wavelet coefficient levels $(l,k)$ and multiplicities $|K_l|=2^l$ from [[def-negative-sobolev-space-for-white-noise]]. The same coefficient-space definition applies to the Haar system used for type-H histograms: detail levels $l\ge0$ have $2^l$ coefficients, and the single scaling coefficient is an additional finite coarsest coordinate, included in the norm with weight $1$. Finite projections always retain that scaling coordinate; this finite convention does not alter any tail assertion. Let $w=(w_l)$ be nondecreasing with $w_l\ge1$. Define
$$M(w)=\left\{x=(x_{lk}):\|x\|_{M(w)}:=\sup_l\frac{\max_{k\in K_l}|x_{lk}|}{w_l}<\infty\right\}$$
and its closed little-o subspace
$$M_0(w)=\left\{x\in M(w):\frac{\max_{k\in K_l}|x_{lk}|}{w_l}\longrightarrow0\text{ as }l\to\infty\right\},$$
with the same norm. Call $w$ admissible when $w_l/\sqrt l\to\infty$. The finite coarsest level is included in the norm and does not affect this limit. Elements are coefficient sequences; in particular, they need not be $L^2$ functions. [[lem-m0w-separable-and-projection-tails]] proves that $M_0(w)$ is a separable Banach space, that $L^2$ coefficient sequences embed in it, and that finite-level projections converge in its norm.

Let $(\psi_{lk})$ be a countable complete orthonormal basis of the real Hilbert space $L^2([0,1])$ ([[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]], [[def-hilbert-space]], [[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]). For a wavelet basis, index levels by $l\ge0$, let $K_l$ have $2^l$ indices, and put $a_l=2^l$ for $l\ge1$ and $a_0=2$ for the finite coarsest level. This finite-level convention only prevents a zero logarithmic weight and does not change any convergence criterion below. For a trigonometric basis, use its integer frequency index $l$, bounded multiplicities, and $a_l=\max(2,|l|)$.

Here an **$S$-regular wavelet basis** means a wavelet orthonormal basis whose members are $S$ times differentiable, with each derivative through order $S$ in $L^2([0,1])$, following the source convention. The weak BvM theorem below only uses the basis's completeness, orthonormality, and level counts.

For $\delta>0$, define $H(\delta)=H^{-1/2,\delta}_2$ to be the space of coefficient sequences $c=(c_{lk})$ with norm

$$\|c\|_{H(\delta)}^2:=\sum_{l,k}a_l^{-1}(\log a_l)^{-2\delta}|c_{lk}|^2<\infty.$$

Its inner product is the corresponding weighted coefficient inner product. Multiplying each coordinate by $a_l^{-1/2}(\log a_l)^{-\delta}$ identifies it isometrically with $\ell^2(I)$, where $I=\{(l,k):k\in K_l\}$ (or the corresponding trigonometric index set). This sequence space is complete: if $x^{(m)}$ is Cauchy, each coordinate converges to a scalar $x_i$; for every finite $F\subset I$, the Cauchy bound passes to the limit in $\sum_{i\in F}|x_i^{(m)}-x_i^{(n)}|^2$, so the supremum over finite $F$ shows $x^{(m)}\to x$ in $\ell^2(I)$. It is separable because finite-support sequences with rational coordinates form a countable dense set. Thus $H(\delta)$ is a separable Hilbert space without an additional choice assumption.

A function $f\in L^2([0,1])$ is identified with its coefficient sequence $c_{lk}=\langle f,\psi_{lk}\rangle$. For each finite set $F$ of indices, orthonormality makes $\sum_{(l,k)\in F}c_{lk}\psi_{lk}$ orthogonal to its residual in $L^2$, so the Pythagorean identity gives $\sum_F|c_{lk}|^2\le\|f\|_2^2$. Taking the supremum over finite $F$ and using the boundedness of the weights proves continuity of the coefficient map. If all coefficients of $f$ vanish, then $f$ is orthogonal to the linear span of the basis. Completeness makes this span dense, and continuity of $g\mapsto\langle f,g\rangle$ gives $\langle f,f\rangle=0$, hence $f=0$ in $L^2$. Applying this to the difference of two functions proves injectivity. Thus the coefficient map is a continuous linear embedding $L^2([0,1])\hookrightarrow H(\delta)$.

The weight trace $\sum_{l,k}a_l^{-1}(\log a_l)^{-2\delta}$ is finite exactly when $\delta>1/2$: for wavelets its tail is a constant multiple of $\sum_{l\ge1}l^{-2\delta}$, while for a trigonometric basis it is comparable to $\sum_{l\ge2}[l(\log l)^{2\delta}]^{-1}$. The product-prior theorem below uses the wavelet case.

derivations.claim: For fixed $t$ and level $l\ge l_0$, a wavelet whose support lies wholly on one side of $t$ contributes zero: it is either disjoint from $[0,t]$ or its entire support is integrated and its mean is zero. Only supports meeting $t$ can contribute. Uniformly bounded overlap bounds their number by a constant, and each coefficient has magnitude at most $\|\psi_{lk}\|_1\le C_0 2^{-l/2}$. Thus $\sup_t\sum_k|\langle1_{[0,t]},\psi_{lk}\rangle|\le C_1 2^{-l/2}$. The finitely many coarsest levels have a finite uniform sum as well.

By [F1] and step 1.1, the absolute sum of all terms at levels $l\ge l_0$ is at most $C_1\|x\|_{M(w)}\sum_{l\ge l_0}w_l2^{-l/2}$, uniformly over $t$. Its tails tend uniformly to zero because $S_w<\infty$. Each finite-level sum is continuous in $t$, since $t\mapsto\int_0^t\psi_{lk}(u)du$ is continuous for an $L^1$ function. The uniform limit is continuous. Applying the same estimate to $x-y$ proves the stated operator-norm bound.

If $x_{lk}=\langle f,\psi_{lk}\rangle$ for $f\in L^2$, the finite orthogonal projections converge to $f$ in $L^2$ by [F2]. The map $f\mapsto\int_0^t f(u)du=\langle f,1_{[0,t]}\rangle$ is a continuous $L^2$ functional because $\|1_{[0,t]}\|_2\le1$. Applying it to the finite projections shows that their coefficient sums converge to $\int_0^t f$, while step 2.1 identifies the same limit with $Jx(t)$.

lem-multiscale-primitive-map-to-continuo.claim:
Let $(\psi_{lk})$ be a compactly supported wavelet basis of [[def-negative-sobolev-space-for-white-noise]]. $$S_w:=\sum_{l\ge l_0}w_l2^{-l/2}<\infty.$$
For $x\in M_0(w)$ define
$$Jx(t):=\sum_{l,k}x_{lk}\langle 1_{[0,t]},\psi_{lk}\rangle_{L^2},\qquad 0\le t\le1.$$

citations.quote:
The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Assume AC. Let $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ be IID on $[0,1]$ with density $0<\rho_0\le f_0\le D_0<\infty$, and suppose $g_0=\log f_0\in C^\alpha$. Use a sufficiently regular compactly supported boundary corrected orthonormal multiresolution wavelet basis satisfying [[lem-compact-wavelet-projection-kernel-and-commutator]], with regularity greater than $\alpha$, and let $V_L$ contain exactly its wavelet levels through $L$, including the fixed low scaling space and constants. Its regularity and vanishing moments satisfy the composition hypotheses in that lemma for some integer $m>\alpha$. Let $L_n$ be either of the two cutoff sequences in [[def-type-s-and-h-multiscale-density-priors]], fixed consistently for all $n$.

In Type-S1 take $\alpha>1$, $\sigma_l=2^{-l(\alpha+1/2)}$, and any coefficient probability density with globally Lipschitz logarithm. In Type-S2 take $\alpha>1/2$, Gaussian coefficients, and $\sigma_l=2^{-l(r+1/2)}$ with $0<r<\alpha-1/4$. Normalize $f=\exp(T)/\int\exp(T)$ as in that definition. For every admissible weight sequence $w$, the posterior satisfies
$$\beta_{BL,M_0(w)}\bigl(\mathcal L(\sqrt n(f-P_n(L_n))\mid X^n),\mathcal L(G_{P_0})\bigr)\longrightarrow0$$
in $P_0^n$-probability, where $P_n(L_n)$ has empirical wavelet coefficients through $L_n$ and zero coefficients above $L_n$, and $G_{P_0}$ is the Borel Gaussian bridge with covariance $P_0[(\psi_i-P_0\psi_i)(\psi_j-P_0\psi_j)]$.

Assume AC. Use the type-H prior of [[def-type-s-and-h-multiscale-density-priors]], retaining its original conditions: $1/2<\alpha\le1$, $f_0\in C^\alpha([0,1])$, $0<\rho_0\le f_0\le D_0<\infty$, either original cutoff $L_n=j_n$ or $L_n=\ell_n$, and $c_1 2^{-L_na}\le a_{k,L_n}\le c_2$ for fixed positive $a,c_1,c_2$. Write $m_n=2^{L_n}$. In the Haar convention, the scaling function is $1$, the detail functions are
$$\psi_{lk}=2^{l/2}(\mathbf1_{I_{l+1,2k}}-\mathbf1_{I_{l+1,2k+1}}),\qquad l\ge0,\quad 0\le k<2^l,$$
and a histogram at resolution $L_n$ has only the scaling coordinate and levels $l<L_n$. Let $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ be IID from $f_0$, let $N_{nk}=\sum_i\mathbf1_{I_{L_n,k}}(X_i)$, and define the empirical histogram
$$h_n(x)=m_n N_{nk}/n\quad\text{on }I_{L_n,k}.$$
Let $\Pi_n(\cdot\mid X^n)$ be the density posterior for the stated histogram prior. For every nondecreasing $w_l\ge1$ with $w_l/\sqrt{l+1}\to\infty$, its conditional law $Q_n$ of $\sqrt n(f-h_n)$ satisfies
$$\beta_{BL,M_0(w)}(Q_n,\mathcal L(G_{P_0}))\longrightarrow0$$
in $P_0^n$-probability, where the Borel centered Gaussian bridge $G_{P_0}$ is supplied by [[lem-density-gaussian-bridge-is-borel-on-m0w]] and has covariance $P_0[(\psi-P_0\psi)(\psi'-P_0\psi')]$. Its scaling coordinate is zero. This proves the type-H source-specific posterior BvM with the empirical projection center; no additional contraction, bias, or Dirichlet-parameter condition is imposed.

Let $V_L$ be the span of wavelets through level $L$ in a compactly supported orthonormal multiresolution basis on $[0,1]$, either boundary corrected or periodized. Assume constants belong to $V_L$, its dimension $d_L\asymp2^L$, and its orthonormal scaling functions $\phi_{Lk}$ have supremum norm at most $C2^{L/2}$, support diameter at most $C2^{-L}$, and uniformly bounded overlap. Periodized supports and distances are interpreted on the circle. Assume also $\sum_k|\psi_{lk}(x)|\le C2^{l/2}$ and $\|\psi_{lk}\|_1\le C2^{-l/2}$. Let $P_L$ denote the orthogonal projection onto $V_L$.

Then $P_L$ has a kernel $K_L$ satisfying $\sup_x\int|K_L(x,y)|dy\le C'$ and $K_L(x,y)=0$ when $\operatorname{dist}(x,y)>C'2^{-L}$. If $a$ is $\beta$-Hölder for $0<\beta\le1$, then
$$\|P_L(ah)-ah\|_\infty\le C'\|a\|_{C^\beta}2^{-\beta L}\|h\|_\infty,\qquad h\in V_L.$$
For the composition assertion, assume additionally an integer $m>\alpha$ such that $\|\psi_{lk}^{(q)}\|_\infty\le C_q2^{l(q+1/2)}$ for $0\le q\le m$, bounded overlap also for their derivatives, and vanishing moments through degree $m-1$ for the detail wavelets, including boundary wavelets; the finite low scaling functions are $C^m$. These are the usual sufficiently regular compact wavelet hypotheses. If a bounded function $g$ has coefficients bounded by $C_g2^{-l(\alpha+1/2)}$, with $\alpha>0$, and its wavelet expansion represents $g$ in $L^2$, then $\|g-P_Lg\|_\infty\le C''C_g2^{-\alpha L}$, up to equality of the continuous representatives. Under these additional derivative and cancellation hypotheses, $e^g$ also has coefficients bounded by $C_g^\prime2^{-l(\alpha+1/2)}$, including integer $\alpha$, and $g,e^g$ are $\beta$-Hölder for every $0<\beta<\min(\alpha,1)$. Moreover $\|h\|_\infty\le C''\sqrt{d_L}\|h\|_2$ for $h\in V_L$.

Assume AC. Let $P_0$ have a density $f_0$ on $[0,1]$ with $\|f_0\|_\infty\le B<\infty$. Let $(\psi_{lk})$ be an orthonormal, compactly supported wavelet basis with $2^l$ coefficients at level $l\ge1$, uniformly bounded overlap, and $\|\psi_{lk}\|_\infty\le C_0 2^{l/2}$. Suppose for some $\gamma>1/2$,
$$\max_k|\langle f_0,\psi_{lk}\rangle|\le C_f2^{-l(\gamma+1/2)}.$$
Let $w_l\ge1$ be nondecreasing and admissible in [[def-multiscale-coefficient-space-m0w]], and choose either cutoff regime
$$2^{L_n}\asymp n^{1/(2\gamma+1)}\quad\text{or}\quad 2^{L_n}\asymp(n/\log n)^{1/(2\gamma+1)}.$$
For IID $X_1,\ldots,X_n\sim P_0$, define the finite wavelet projection $P_n(L_n)$ by coefficients $\langle P_n(L_n),\psi_{lk}\rangle=P_n\psi_{lk}:=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\psi_{lk}(X_i)$ for $l\le L_n$ and zero for $l>L_n$, with the coarsest scaling coordinates projected as well. Let $G_{P_0}$ be a Borel centered Gaussian law on $M_0(w)$ whose coefficient covariance is
$$\operatorname{Cov}(G_{lk},G_{l'k'})=P_0[(\psi_{lk}-P_0\psi_{lk})(\psi_{l'k'}-P_0\psi_{l'k'})].$$
Then
$$\sqrt n\{P_n(L_n)-f_0\}\Rightarrow G_{P_0}\quad\text{in }M_0(w).$$

Assume AC. Let $P_0$ have density $0<\rho\le f_0\le D<\infty$ on $[0,1]$, and put $F_0(t)=\int_0^t f_0$. Use a complete real orthonormal wavelet basis, allowing the Haar basis with its finite scaling coordinate, and admissible weights $w$ as in [[def-multiscale-coefficient-space-m0w]]. Assume the wavelet geometry and summability conditions of [[lem-multiscale-primitive-map-to-continuous-cdfs]], and write $J:M_0(w)\to C([0,1])$ for its primitive map. Let $G$ be the Borel centered Gaussian bridge random element of [[lem-density-gaussian-bridge-is-borel-on-m0w]], with coefficient covariance
$$\operatorname{Cov}(G_{lk},G_{l'k'})=P_0[(\psi_{lk}-P_0\psi_{lk})(\psi_{l'k'}-P_0\psi_{l'k'})].$$
Then the distribution functions of $\|G\|_{M(w)}$ and $\|JG\|_\infty$ are continuous on $\mathbb R$ and strictly increasing on $(0,\infty)$. Both assign probability zero to $0$, and take values strictly between $0$ and $1$ at every positive argument. Consequently, for every $u\in(0,1)$, each has a unique positive finite lower $u$-quantile $q$, with CDF value $u$, and is strictly increasing on an open neighborhood of $q$.

Let $P_0$ have a density $f_0$ on $[0,1]$ bounded above and bounded away from zero, and put $F_0(t)=\int_0^t f_0(x)dx$. Use the wavelet basis and $M_0(w)$ of [[def-multiscale-coefficient-space-m0w]], and assume the wavelet conditions and summability condition $\sum_lw_l2^{-l/2}<\infty$ of [[lem-multiscale-primitive-map-to-continuous-cdfs]]. Let $T_n$ be a measurable $L^2$-valued center, let $\Pi_n$ be a posterior kernel supported on $L^2$ densities, and define $Q_n$ to be the conditional law on $M_0(w)$ of $\sqrt n(f-T_n)$ under $f\sim\Pi_n(\cdot\mid X^n)$.

Assume under $P_0^n$ that (i) $Q_n$ converges in bounded-Lipschitz distance in probability to the centered Gaussian bridge coefficient law $G_{P_0}$ in $M_0(w)$, whose finite coefficient covariances are $P_0[(h-P_0h)(g-P_0g)]$, and (ii) $\sqrt n(T_n-f_0)\Rightarrow G_{P_0}$ in $M_0(w)$. For $u=1-\alpha$, let $q_M$ and $q_C$ be the lower $u$-quantiles of $\|G_{P_0}\|_{M(w)}$ and $\|JG_{P_0}\|_\infty$. Assume both CDFs are continuous on $\mathbb R$ and strictly increasing on open neighborhoods of their respective quantiles, and that $q_M,q_C>0$. These local quantile conditions allow the CDFs to be constant on the negative half-line. In the projected empirical-center case $T_n=P_n(L_n)$, [[thm-projected-empirical-process-clt-in-m0w]] supplies premise (ii) under its stated smoothness and cutoff conditions. For the source-specific type-S and type-H priors, the posterior BvM premise (i) is established in [[thm-type-s-density-weak-bvm-on-m0w]] and [[thm-type-h-histogram-posterior-weak-bvm-in-m0w]], respectively.

For a posterior draw $f$, write $F_f=Jf$ and $F_{T_n}=JT_n$, where $J$ is the primitive map of [[lem-multiscale-primitive-map-to-continuous-cdfs]]. Then the posterior law of $\sqrt n(F_f-F_{T_n})$ converges in bounded-Lipschitz distance on $C([0,1])$ to the $P_0$-Brownian bridge $B_{P_0}(t)$, with covariance $F_0(s\wedge t)-F_0(s)F_0(t)$.

For $0<\alpha<1$, let $R_n^M$ and $R_n^C$ be the posterior lower $1-\alpha$ quantiles of $\|\sqrt n(f-T_n)\|_{M(w)}$ and $\|\sqrt n(F_f-F_{T_n})\|_\infty$, respectively. The corresponding posterior balls
$$C_n^M=\{f:\|f-T_n\|_{M(w)}\le R_n^M/\sqrt n\},\qquad C_n^C=\{F:\|F-F_{T_n}\|_\infty\le R_n^C/\sqrt n\}$$
are measurable credible sets of posterior mass at least $1-\alpha$. Their frequentist coverage tends to $1-\alpha$, and the scaled radii converge to the respective $1-\alpha$ quantiles of $\|G_{P_0}\|_{M(w)}$ and $\|B_{P_0}\|_\infty$.

Use the $M_0(w)$ credible ball $C_n^M$ and radius $R_n^M$ of [[thm-cdf-and-multiscale-credible-band-calibration-from-bvm]]. Let $\gamma>0$, assume the compactly supported wavelets have uniformly bounded overlap and $\|\psi_{lk}\|_\infty\le C2^{l/2}$, and define
$$\|f\|_{C^\gamma_\psi}:=\sup_{l,k}2^{l(\gamma+1/2)}|\langle f,\psi_{lk}\rangle|.$$
Suppose $\|f_0\|_{C^\gamma_\psi}<\infty$. Choose integers $j_n$ with $2^{j_n}\asymp(n/\log n)^{1/(2\gamma+1)}$ and let $u_n=w_{j_n}/\sqrt{j_n}\to\infty$. Intersect the credible ball with the coefficient smoothness ball:
$$\overline C_n=C_n^M\cap\{f:\|f\|_{C^\gamma_\psi}\le u_n\}.$$
Then $P_{f_0}^{(n)}\{f_0\in\overline C_n\}\to1-\alpha$, and its $L^\infty$ diameter satisfies
$$\operatorname{diam}_{L^\infty}(\overline C_n)=O_{P_{f_0}^{(n)}}\!\left((n/\log n)^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+1)}u_n\right).$$

derivations.claim: In Type S, [F1] proves posterior BvM about $T_n=P_n(L_n)$ with the original S1 range $\alpha>1$ and original Gaussian S2 range $\alpha>1/2$, $0<r<\alpha-1/4$. The truth $g_0=\log f_0$ has $\alpha$ coefficient regularity, so [F2] gives that regularity for $f_0=e^{g_0}$ as well. The retained basis has the support, overlap and supremum bounds required by the empirical-process theorem in [F2]. Taking $\gamma=\alpha>1/2$ and the given cutoff therefore proves its sampling-center CLT with the same Gaussian bridge.

In Type H, [F1] proves posterior BvM about the empirical histogram $h_n$. Haar wavelets have the same support, overlap and supremum bounds. The ordinary $\alpha$-Hölder truth, $1/2<\alpha\le1$, has Haar coefficients bounded by $C2^{-l(\alpha+1/2)}$: subtract its value at one point of the support in the coefficient integral, use the zero mean, support diameter $2^{-l}$ and $L^1$ norm $2^{-l/2}$. The histogram projection retains details through $J_n=L_n-1$. Both given cutoff regimes remain true with this $J_n$, since multiplying $2^{L_n}$ by $1/2$ changes only their comparison constants. Thus [F2] with $\gamma=\alpha$ gives the sampling CLT about this exact histogram center. The finite scaling coordinate is included and its centered fluctuation is zero.

In all three cases, positivity and boundedness of $f_0$, admissibility, and the displayed summability verify [F3]. Hence every norm-quantile assumption of [F4] holds at $u=1-\eta$. Steps 1.1–1.2 verify its posterior and sampling premises, with the same coefficient covariance law. Applying [F4] proves all asserted CDF limits, measurable credibility, radius limits and frequentist coverage, for the exact empirical centers and every $0<\eta<1$.

When the additional hypotheses in the last paragraph of the Statement hold, the multiscale credible ball just obtained is precisely the input to [F5]. Applying that theorem yields its smoothness-intersection coverage and stated diameter rate. These are additional hypotheses only for this diameter conclusion; the coverage and CDF conclusions in step 2.1 required no such extra conditions.

boundaries.reason: The sampling truth is a probability density on [0,1], so the model is nonempty.

boundaries.evidence: The bridge norm quantile supplier proves strictly positive finite interior radii; the deterministic scaling coordinate is allowed to be zero.
The uniform density example verifies all premises and both specific prior constructions.
Credibility level has 0<eta<1; smoothness/range/cutoff endpoints remain exactly the cited supplier hypotheses.
Full AC is explicit and inherited from the density bridge, posterior BvM and finite sampling CLT suppliers.

cor-type-s-h-density-credible-band-calib.finite_check_disposition: No finite smoke obligation; this is a direct application of the fully proved local suppliers.
cor-type-s-h-density-credible-band-calib.claim:
Assume AC. Use either Type-S1, Type-S2 or Type-H with all the truth, basis, prior-scale, Dirichlet-parameter and cutoff conditions of [[def-type-s-and-h-multiscale-density-priors]]. Let $w_l\ge1$ be nondecreasing, $w_l/\sqrt{l+1}\to\infty$, and $\sum_lw_l2^{-l/2}<\infty$. In Type S take $T_n=P_n(L_n)$, the empirical wavelet projection through level $L_n$. In Type H take the empirical histogram $T_n=h_n$ at mesh $2^{-L_n}$, equivalently the Haar projection with scaling coordinate and details $l<L_n$.

For each $0<\eta<1$, the posterior multiscale and CDF balls of [[thm-cdf-and-multiscale-credible-band-calibration-from-bvm]], at posterior level $1-\eta$ and centered at these $T_n$, have posterior mass at least $1-\eta$ and frequentist coverage tending to $1-\eta$. Their scaled radii converge in probability to the positive finite $1-\eta$ quantiles of the corresponding Gaussian bridge norms. In particular the CDF posterior converges in bounded-Lipschitz distance to the $P_0$-Brownian bridge law.

If additionally the coefficient smoothness and undersmoothing hypotheses of [[thm-multiscale-credible-band-holder-diameter]] hold, its intersection with the stated coefficient smoothness ball has the same limiting coverage and the diameter bound asserted there. No unverified entropy, prior-mass, posterior contraction or quantile-regularity premise is required in this corollary.

manifest_rows.title: Density normal laws and square-summable Gaussian series under countable choice
manifest_rows.statement:
Assume countable choice. Put $g(x)=(2\pi)^{-1/2}e^{-x^2/2}$. Then $\gamma(E)=\int_Eg(x)\,dx$ is a Borel probability on $\mathbb R$. In this item and its applications, write $N(m,v)$ for its pushforward under $x\mapsto m+\sqrt v\,x$, where $v\ge0$; thus $N(m,0)=\delta_m$. This density convention requires no full axiom of choice. For $v>0$ the law has density
$$g_{m,v}(x)=(2\pi v)^{-1/2}\exp\{- (x-m)^2/(2v)\},$$
and its CDF is continuous and strictly increasing. Its mean and variance are $m$ and $v$.

If $Z_j$ are mutually independent with density $g$ and $\sum_{j\ge1}c_j^2=v<\infty$, and the finite sums $S_m=\sum_{j\le m}c_jZ_j$ converge in probability to a supplied real random variable $S$, then $S$ has law $N(0,v)$. In particular, this applies whenever the sums converge almost surely or in $L^2$.

references.title: Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, fifth edition, Gaussian density and independent sums

manifest_rows.title: White noise is a Borel Gaussian law on the negative Sobolev space
manifest_rows.statement: Assume countable choice. Let $(\psi_{lk})$ be the wavelet or trigonometric basis from [[def-negative-sobolev-space-for-white-noise]]. Let $Z_{lk}$ be mutually independent real random variables with density $g(x)=(2\pi)^{-1/2}e^{-x^2/2}$. Define the formal white-noise coefficient sequence $W=(Z_{lk})$. For every $\delta>1/2$, this sequence is almost surely an element of $H(\delta)$ and is a Borel Gaussian random element there. Its law $N$ is a Borel probability on $H(\delta)$. For an infinite-dimensional basis, white noise is not an $L^2([0,1])$-valued random element. Here Gaussian means that each continuous real linear functional has a centered law $N(0,v)$ in the density convention of [[lem-density-normal-laws-and-square-summable-gaussian-series]]; in particular, for $L(c)=\sum_jd_jc_j$ its variance is $\sum_jd_j^2$ whenever this pairing is continuous on $H(\delta)$.

references.title: Castillo and Nickl, Nonparametric Bernstein–von Mises theorems in Gaussian white noise, §1.2, equations (7)–(8), printed pp. 2005–2006
Giné and Nickl, Mathematical Foundations of Infinite-Dimensional Statistical Models, §7.3.4, printed pp. 594–595
Ray, Adaptive Bernstein–von Mises theorems in Gaussian white noise, §2.1, printed pp. 5–6

manifest_rows.title: Prior-predictive and fixed-truth data laws are equivalent
manifest_rows.statement: Assume countable choice. Use the wavelet product prior and white-noise model from [[lem-wavelet-product-prior-is-l2-valued]] and [[lem-white-noise-is-borel-gaussian-on-negative-sobolev-space]], with $\alpha>0$, $\sigma_l=2^{-l(\alpha+1/2)}$, and a common coefficient density $\varphi$ having finite second moment $m_2$. Let $f_0\in L^2([0,1])$. For each $n\ge1$ and $\delta>1/2$, let $Q_n$ be the prior-predictive law on $H(\delta)$ of $X=f+n^{-1/2}W$, with prior draw $f$ independent of canonical white noise $W$, and let $P_{f_0}^{(n)}$ be the law of $f_0+n^{-1/2}W$. Then $Q_n$ and $P_{f_0}^{(n)}$ are mutually absolutely continuous as Borel probabilities on $H(\delta)$.

references.title: Castillo and Nickl, Nonparametric Bernstein–von Mises theorems in Gaussian white noise, Condition 1 and Theorem 5, printed pp. 2013–2016
Giné and Nickl, Mathematical Foundations of Infinite-Dimensional Statistical Models, Condition 7.3.11 and Theorem 7.3.12, printed pp. 583–586

manifest_rows.title: Weak nonparametric Bernstein–von Mises theorem for product priors
manifest_rows.statement:
Let $(\psi_{lk})$ be the S-regular wavelet basis in [[def-negative-sobolev-space-for-white-noise]], with $2^l$ coefficients at each level $l\ge0$. For $\alpha>0$, put $\sigma_l=2^{-l(\alpha+1/2)}$ and let the prior on $f=\sum_{l,k}\sigma_l\xi_{lk}\psi_{lk}$ have IID coefficients $\xi_{lk}$ with density $\varphi$. Assume countable choice for the $L^2$ prior construction supplied by [[lem-wavelet-product-prior-is-l2-valued]], and take the full posterior kernel as the supplied model input of [[lem-product-prior-coordinate-posterior-law]]. Let $f_0\in L^2([0,1])$, write $\theta_{0,lk}=\langle f_0,\psi_{lk}\rangle$ and $r_{lk}=\theta_{0,lk}/\sigma_l$, and suppose

$$\sup_{l,k}|r_{lk}|\le M<\tau,$$

where $\varphi$ is a probability density satisfying $\varphi(u)\le C_\varphi$ for every $u$, $\varphi(u)\ge c_\varphi>0$ for $|u|<\tau$, $\int u^2\varphi(u)\,du<\infty$, and $\varphi$ is continuous at each $r_{lk}$. The observation model is

$$dX^{(n)}(t)=f_0(t)\,dt+n^{-1/2}dW(t),\qquad 0\le t\le1,$$

with standard white noise $W$; in the stated basis this is the sequence experiment $X_{lk}=\theta_{0,lk}+n^{-1/2}Z_{lk}$ with independent standard normal coordinates. Let $\Pi_n(\cdot\mid X)$ be the product-coordinate posterior of [[lem-product-prior-coordinate-posterior-law]]. Let $N$ be the law of the canonical white noise in $H(\delta)$ and define

$$\widetilde\Pi_n:=\Pi_n(\cdot\mid X)\circ[f\mapsto\sqrt n(f-X)]^{-1},\qquad \beta_{BL,H(\delta)}(\mu,\nu):=\sup_{\substack{\|g\|_\infty\le1\\ \operatorname{Lip}_{H(\delta)}(g)\le1}}\left|\int g\,d\mu-\int g\,d\nu\right|.$$

For every $\delta>1/2$,

$$\beta_{BL,H(\delta)}(\widetilde\Pi_n,N)\longrightarrow0$$

in probability under the true white-noise law $P_{f_0}^{(n)}$. This is a bounded-Lipschitz weak BvM conclusion; it asserts neither total-variation convergence on all Borel subsets nor an $L^2$-valued Gaussian limit.

references.title: Castillo and Nickl, Nonparametric Bernstein–von Mises theorems in Gaussian white noise, Theorems 5, 7–9 and proofs, printed pp. 2013–2021
Giné and Nickl, Mathematical Foundations of Infinite-Dimensional Statistical Models, Theorems 7.3.12, 7.3.18–7.3.19 and proofs, printed pp. 584–596
Ray, Adaptive Bernstein–von Mises theorems in Gaussian white noise, §§2.1–2.2 and §7.1, printed pp. 5–8 and 23–24

manifest_rows.title: The scaled posterior converges weakly on the negative Sobolev space
manifest_rows.statement: Assume AC and the hypotheses of [[thm-weak-nonparametric-bernstein-von-mises-for-product-priors]]. Then the random Borel probability measures $\widetilde\Pi_n$ converge weakly in probability to $N$ on $H(\delta)$, where weak convergence is the bounded-continuous-test definition in [[def-weak-convergence-of-borel-probability-measures]].

references.title: Castillo and Nickl, Nonparametric Bernstein–von Mises theorems in Gaussian white noise, Definition 1 and Theorem 9, printed pp. 2003–2004 and 2019–2020
Giné and Nickl, Mathematical Foundations of Infinite-Dimensional Statistical Models, Theorem 7.3.19, printed pp. 595–596

manifest_rows.title: Linear-functional BvM limit and credible-interval calibration
manifest_rows.statement:
Use the product-prior white-noise model and supplied posterior kernel of [[thm-weak-nonparametric-bernstein-von-mises-for-product-priors]], including its wavelet-basis, coefficient-density, truth, and countable-choice hypotheses. Let $g\in H^s_2$ for some $s>1/2$, with $g\ne0$, and put $\sigma_g=\|g\|_2$. Let $Q_n$ be the posterior law of $L_g(f)$ and let
$$C_{n,\alpha}=\left[q_{\alpha/2}(Q_n),q_{1-\alpha/2}(Q_n)\right],\qquad 0<\alpha<1.$$
Then
$$\beta_{BL,\mathbb R}\!\left(Q_n\circ[u\mapsto\sqrt n(u-L_g(X^{(n)}))]^{-1},N(0,\sigma_g^2)\right)\longrightarrow0$$
in $P_{f_0}^{(n)}$-probability. The interval $C_{n,\alpha}$ is posterior credible at level $1-\alpha$, and its frequentist coverage satisfies
$$P_{f_0}^{(n)}\{L_g(f_0)\in C_{n,\alpha}\}\longrightarrow1-\alpha.$$

references.title: Castillo and Nickl, Nonparametric Bernstein–von Mises theorems in Gaussian white noise, Theorem 3 and §2.3.1
Giné and Nickl, Mathematical Foundations of Infinite-Dimensional Statistical Models, §§7.3.4–7.3.5

manifest_rows.title: Nonlinear-functional BvM limit under fast L2 contraction
manifest_rows.statement:
Use the white-noise experiment, product prior, and supplied posterior kernel of [[thm-weak-nonparametric-bernstein-von-mises-for-product-priors]], with all its stated basis, coefficient-density, truth, and countable-choice hypotheses. Let $\Psi:L^2([0,1])\to\mathbb R$ be Borel measurable. Suppose $f_0\in L^2$, and for some $g\in H^s_2$, $s>1/2$, $g\ne0$, $C<\infty$, and $\rho>0$,
$$|\Psi(f_0+h)-\Psi(f_0)-\langle h,g\rangle_{L^2}|\le C\|h\|_2^2\quad\text{whenever }\|h\|_2\le\rho.$$
Assume the posterior contracts in $L^2$ at a deterministic radius $r_n=o(n^{-1/2})$, meaning $\Pi_n(\|f-f_0\|_2>r_n\mid X^{(n)})=o_{P_{f_0}^{(n)}}(1)$. Define the efficient center
$$\theta_n^*:=\Psi(f_0)+L_g(X^{(n)}-f_0),$$
where the last pairing is the continuous $H(\delta)$ extension from [[lem-smooth-functional-extends-to-negative-sobolev-space]]. Then the posterior law of $\sqrt n\{\Psi(f)-\theta_n^*\}$ converges in bounded-Lipschitz distance to $N(0,\|g\|_2^2)$ in $P_{f_0}^{(n)}$-probability. The equal-tailed posterior interval for $\Psi(f)$ at level $1-\alpha$ is credible and has frequentist coverage tending to $1-\alpha$.

The radius assumption is the stronger convention required by this plan. It implies the source's squared-radius condition: with $s_n=r_n^2$, one has $s_n=o(n^{-1/2})$ and posterior mass inside $\|f-f_0\|_2^2\le s_n$ tends to one.

references.title: Castillo and Nickl, Nonparametric Bernstein–von Mises theorems in Gaussian white noise, Theorem 4 and §2.3.2
Giné and Nickl, Mathematical Foundations of Infinite-Dimensional Statistical Models, §§7.3.4–7.3.5

manifest_rows.title: Logarithmic negative Sobolev spaces for white noise
manifest_rows.statement:
Let $(\psi_{lk})$ be a countable complete orthonormal basis of the real Hilbert space $L^2([0,1])$ ([[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]], [[def-hilbert-space]], [[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]). For a wavelet basis, index levels by $l\ge0$, let $K_l$ have $2^l$ indices, and put $a_l=2^l$ for $l\ge1$ and $a_0=2$ for the finite coarsest level. This finite-level convention only prevents a zero logarithmic weight and does not change any convergence criterion below. For a trigonometric basis, use its integer frequency index $l$, bounded multiplicities, and $a_l=\max(2,|l|)$.

Here an **$S$-regular wavelet basis** means a wavelet orthonormal basis whose members are $S$ times differentiable, with each derivative through order $S$ in $L^2([0,1])$, following the source convention. The weak BvM theorem below only uses the basis's completeness, orthonormality, and level counts.

For $\delta>0$, define $H(\delta)=H^{-1/2,\delta}_2$ to be the space of coefficient sequences $c=(c_{lk})$ with norm

$$\|c\|_{H(\delta)}^2:=\sum_{l,k}a_l^{-1}(\log a_l)^{-2\delta}|c_{lk}|^2<\infty.$$

Its inner product is the corresponding weighted coefficient inner product. Multiplying each coordinate by $a_l^{-1/2}(\log a_l)^{-\delta}$ identifies it isometrically with $\ell^2(I)$, where $I=\{(l,k):k\in K_l\}$ (or the corresponding trigonometric index set). This sequence space is complete: if $x^{(m)}$ is Cauchy, each coordinate converges to a scalar $x_i$; for every finite $F\subset I$, the Cauchy bound passes to the limit in $\sum_{i\in F}|x_i^{(m)}-x_i^{(n)}|^2$, so the supremum over finite $F$ shows $x^{(m)}\to x$ in $\ell^2(I)$. It is separable because finite-support sequences with rational coordinates form a countable dense set. Thus $H(\delta)$ is a separable Hilbert space without an additional choice assumption.

A function $f\in L^2([0,1])$ is identified with its coefficient sequence $c_{lk}=\langle f,\psi_{lk}\rangle$. For each finite set $F$ of indices, orthonormality makes $\sum_{(l,k)\in F}c_{lk}\psi_{lk}$ orthogonal to its residual in $L^2$, so the Pythagorean identity gives $\sum_F|c_{lk}|^2\le\|f\|_2^2$. Taking the supremum over finite $F$ and using the boundedness of the weights proves continuity of the coefficient map. If all coefficients of $f$ vanish, then $f$ is orthogonal to the linear span of the basis. Completeness makes this span dense, and continuity of $g\mapsto\langle f,g\rangle$ gives $\langle f,f\rangle=0$, hence $f=0$ in $L^2$. Applying this to the difference of two functions proves injectivity. Thus the coefficient map is a continuous linear embedding $L^2([0,1])\hookrightarrow H(\delta)$.

The weight trace $\sum_{l,k}a_l^{-1}(\log a_l)^{-2\delta}$ is finite exactly when $\delta>1/2$: for wavelets its tail is a constant multiple of $\sum_{l\ge1}l^{-2\delta}$, while for a trigonometric basis it is comparable to $\sum_{l\ge2}[l(\log l)^{2\delta}]^{-1}$. The product-prior theorem below uses the wavelet case.

references.title: Castillo and Nickl, Nonparametric Bernstein–von Mises theorems in Gaussian white noise, Definition 2 and equations (7)–(8), printed pp. 2004–2006
Giné and Nickl, Mathematical Foundations of Infinite-Dimensional Statistical Models, §7.3.4, printed pp. 594–595

manifest_rows.title: The bounded-Lipschitz metric characterizes weak convergence on Polish spaces
manifest_rows.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $(S,d)$ be a Polish space, and let $\mu_n,\mu$ be Borel probability measures on $S$. Define

$$\beta_{BL}(\nu,\rho):=\sup\left\{\left|\int g\,d\nu-\int g\,d\rho\right|:g:S\to\mathbb R,\ \|g\|_\infty\le1,\ \operatorname{Lip}_d(g)\le1\right\},$$

where $\operatorname{Lip}_d(g):=\sup_{x\ne y}|g(x)-g(y)|/d(x,y)$, with value $0$ when $S$ has at most one point. Then

$$\mu_n\Rightarrow\mu\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\beta_{BL}(\mu_n,\mu)\longrightarrow0,$$

where $\Rightarrow$ is weak convergence of Borel probabilities ([[def-weak-convergence-of-borel-probability-measures]]). The implication from bounded-Lipschitz convergence to weak convergence is choice-free; the reverse implication below uses AC through Prokhorov's theorem.

references.title: Giné and Nickl, Mathematical Foundations of Infinite-Dimensional Statistical Models, §3.7 and §7.3.4, printed pp. 246–247 and 594–595
Castillo and Nickl, Nonparametric Bernstein–von Mises theorems in Gaussian white noise, Definition 1, printed pp. 2003–2004

manifest_rows.title: CDF and multiscale credible-band calibration from weak BvM limits
manifest_rows.statement:
Let $P_0$ have a density $f_0$ on $[0,1]$ bounded above and bounded away from zero, and put $F_0(t)=\int_0^t f_0(x)dx$. Use the wavelet basis and $M_0(w)$ of [[def-multiscale-coefficient-space-m0w]], and assume the wavelet conditions and summability condition $\sum_lw_l2^{-l/2}<\infty$ of [[lem-multiscale-primitive-map-to-continuous-cdfs]]. Let $T_n$ be a measurable $L^2$-valued center, let $\Pi_n$ be a posterior kernel supported on $L^2$ densities, and define $Q_n$ to be the conditional law on $M_0(w)$ of $\sqrt n(f-T_n)$ under $f\sim\Pi_n(\cdot\mid X^n)$.

Assume under $P_0^n$ that (i) $Q_n$ converges in bounded-Lipschitz distance in probability to the centered Gaussian bridge coefficient law $G_{P_0}$ in $M_0(w)$, whose finite coefficient covariances are $P_0[(h-P_0h)(g-P_0g)]$, and (ii) $\sqrt n(T_n-f_0)\Rightarrow G_{P_0}$ in $M_0(w)$. For $u=1-\alpha$, let $q_M$ and $q_C$ be the lower $u$-quantiles of $\|G_{P_0}\|_{M(w)}$ and $\|JG_{P_0}\|_\infty$. Assume both CDFs are continuous on $\mathbb R$ and strictly increasing on open neighborhoods of their respective quantiles, and that $q_M,q_C>0$. These local quantile conditions allow the CDFs to be constant on the negative half-line. In the projected empirical-center case $T_n=P_n(L_n)$, [[thm-projected-empirical-process-clt-in-m0w]] supplies premise (ii) under its stated smoothness and cutoff conditions. For the source-specific type-S and type-H priors, the posterior BvM premise (i) is established in [[thm-type-s-density-weak-bvm-on-m0w]] and [[thm-type-h-histogram-posterior-weak-bvm-in-m0w]], respectively.

For a posterior draw $f$, write $F_f=Jf$ and $F_{T_n}=JT_n$, where $J$ is the primitive map of [[lem-multiscale-primitive-map-to-continuous-cdfs]]. Then the posterior law of $\sqrt n(F_f-F_{T_n})$ converges in bounded-Lipschitz distance on $C([0,1])$ to the $P_0$-Brownian bridge $B_{P_0}(t)$, with covariance $F_0(s\wedge t)-F_0(s)F_0(t)$.

For $0<\alpha<1$, let $R_n^M$ and $R_n^C$ be the posterior lower $1-\alpha$ quantiles of $\|\sqrt n(f-T_n)\|_{M(w)}$ and $\|\sqrt n(F_f-F_{T_n})\|_\infty$, respectively. The corresponding posterior balls
$$C_n^M=\{f:\|f-T_n\|_{M(w)}\le R_n^M/\sqrt n\},\qquad C_n^C=\{F:\|F-F_{T_n}\|_\infty\le R_n^C/\sqrt n\}$$
are measurable credible sets of posterior mass at least $1-\alpha$. Their frequentist coverage tends to $1-\alpha$, and the scaled radii converge to the respective $1-\alpha$ quantiles of $\|G_{P_0}\|_{M(w)}$ and $\|B_{P_0}\|_\infty$.

references.title: Castillo and Nickl, On the Bernstein–von Mises phenomenon for nonparametric Bayes procedures, Theorems 4–5, Corollary 2, and §5.4
Giné and Nickl, Mathematical Foundations of Infinite-Dimensional Statistical Models, Theorem 7.3.23 and proof

manifest_rows.title: Continuous and strictly increasing norm distributions for density bridges
manifest_rows.statement:
Assume AC. Let $P_0$ have density $0<\rho\le f_0\le D<\infty$ on $[0,1]$, and put $F_0(t)=\int_0^t f_0$. Use a complete real orthonormal wavelet basis, allowing the Haar basis with its finite scaling coordinate, and admissible weights $w$ as in [[def-multiscale-coefficient-space-m0w]]. Assume the wavelet geometry and summability conditions of [[lem-multiscale-primitive-map-to-continuous-cdfs]], and write $J:M_0(w)\to C([0,1])$ for its primitive map. Let $G$ be the Borel centered Gaussian bridge random element of [[lem-density-gaussian-bridge-is-borel-on-m0w]], with coefficient covariance
$$\operatorname{Cov}(G_{lk},G_{l'k'})=P_0[(\psi_{lk}-P_0\psi_{lk})(\psi_{l'k'}-P_0\psi_{l'k'})].$$
Then the distribution functions of $\|G\|_{M(w)}$ and $\|JG\|_\infty$ are continuous on $\mathbb R$ and strictly increasing on $(0,\infty)$. Both assign probability zero to $0$, and take values strictly between $0$ and $1$ at every positive argument. Consequently, for every $u\in(0,1)$, each has a unique positive finite lower $u$-quantile $q$, with CDF value $u$, and is strictly increasing on an open neighborhood of $q$.

references.title: Castillo and Nickl, On the Bernstein–von Mises phenomenon for nonparametric Bayes procedures, Theorems 4–5 and Section 4
Rick Durrett, Probability: Theory and Examples, fifth edition, Sections 7.4 and 8.4

manifest_rows.title: A bounded-density Gaussian bridge has a Borel multiscale law
manifest_rows.statement:
Assume AC. Let $P_0$ have density $0\le f_0\le D<\infty$ on $[0,1]$, and let $(\psi_{lk})$ be an orthonormal wavelet system with at most $C2^l$ coordinates per level, including finitely many coarsest scaling coordinates. The Haar system is allowed. For every admissible $w$, there exists a Borel centered Gaussian random element $G_{P_0}$ of $M_0(w)$ with coefficient covariance
$$K((l,k),(l',k'))=P_0[(\psi_{lk}-P_0\psi_{lk})(\psi_{l'k'}-P_0\psi_{l'k'})].$$
Its Borel law is uniquely determined by these finite-coordinate Gaussian laws.

references.title: Castillo and Nickl, On the Bernstein–von Mises phenomenon for nonparametric Bayes procedures, §2.1 and Theorem 1

manifest_rows.title: Finite Dirichlet gamma representation and weighted Bernstein bound
manifest_rows.statement:
Assume AC. Let $\beta_1,\ldots,\beta_m>0$, $B=\sum_j\beta_j$, and let $Z_j$ be independent $\operatorname{Gamma}(\beta_j,1)$ variables. Put $S=\sum_j Z_j$. Then $\omega=(Z_j/S)_j$ is $\operatorname{Dirichlet}(\beta_1,\ldots,\beta_m)$, and $S$ is $\operatorname{Gamma}(B,1)$, with mean $B$ and variance $B$. Each $Z_j$ has mean $\beta_j$, variance $\beta_j$, and moment-generating function $\mathbb E e^{uZ_j}=(1-u)^{-\beta_j}$ for every real $u<1$. For real $q_j$ satisfying $|q_j|\le b$, put $T(q)=\sum_jq_j(Z_j-\beta_j)$ and $V=\sum_j\beta_jq_j^2$. If $V>0$, then for $x>0$,
$$\Pr\{|T(q)|>x\}\le2\exp\left\{-\frac{x^2}{2(V+bx)}\right\}.$$
If $V=0$, $T(q)=0$ almost surely. Sums of disjoint groups of the $Z_j$ are independent Gamma variables with their respective summed shapes.

references.title: Castillo, On Bayesian supremum norm contraction rates, §4.4
Ferguson, A Bayesian Analysis of Some Nonparametric Problems, Section 2

manifest_rows.title: Type-H histogram posterior weak Bernstein–von Mises theorem
manifest_rows.statement:
Assume AC. Use the type-H prior of [[def-type-s-and-h-multiscale-density-priors]], retaining its original conditions: $1/2<\alpha\le1$, $f_0\in C^\alpha([0,1])$, $0<\rho_0\le f_0\le D_0<\infty$, either original cutoff $L_n=j_n$ or $L_n=\ell_n$, and $c_1 2^{-L_na}\le a_{k,L_n}\le c_2$ for fixed positive $a,c_1,c_2$. Write $m_n=2^{L_n}$. In the Haar convention, the scaling function is $1$, the detail functions are
$$\psi_{lk}=2^{l/2}(\mathbf1_{I_{l+1,2k}}-\mathbf1_{I_{l+1,2k+1}}),\qquad l\ge0,\quad 0\le k<2^l,$$
and a histogram at resolution $L_n$ has only the scaling coordinate and levels $l<L_n$. Let $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ be IID from $f_0$, let $N_{nk}=\sum_i\mathbf1_{I_{L_n,k}}(X_i)$, and define the empirical histogram
$$h_n(x)=m_n N_{nk}/n\quad\text{on }I_{L_n,k}.$$
Let $\Pi_n(\cdot\mid X^n)$ be the density posterior for the stated histogram prior. For every nondecreasing $w_l\ge1$ with $w_l/\sqrt{l+1}\to\infty$, its conditional law $Q_n$ of $\sqrt n(f-h_n)$ satisfies
$$\beta_{BL,M_0(w)}(Q_n,\mathcal L(G_{P_0}))\longrightarrow0$$
in $P_0^n$-probability, where the Borel centered Gaussian bridge $G_{P_0}$ is supplied by [[lem-density-gaussian-bridge-is-borel-on-m0w]] and has covariance $P_0[(\psi-P_0\psi)(\psi'-P_0\psi')]$. Its scaling coordinate is zero. This proves the type-H source-specific posterior BvM with the empirical projection center; no additional contraction, bias, or Dirichlet-parameter condition is imposed.

references.title: Castillo and Nickl, On the Bernstein–von Mises phenomenon for nonparametric Bayes procedures, Theorem 3 and §5.4, printed pp.24–28
Castillo, On Bayesian supremum norm contraction rates, §4.4, printed pp.25–28

manifest_rows.title: Compact wavelet projections approximate smooth functions and commute asymptotically with multiplication
manifest_rows.statement:
Let $V_L$ be the span of wavelets through level $L$ in a compactly supported orthonormal multiresolution basis on $[0,1]$, either boundary corrected or periodized. Assume constants belong to $V_L$, its dimension $d_L\asymp2^L$, and its orthonormal scaling functions $\phi_{Lk}$ have supremum norm at most $C2^{L/2}$, support diameter at most $C2^{-L}$, and uniformly bounded overlap. Periodized supports and distances are interpreted on the circle. Assume also $\sum_k|\psi_{lk}(x)|\le C2^{l/2}$ and $\|\psi_{lk}\|_1\le C2^{-l/2}$. Let $P_L$ denote the orthogonal projection onto $V_L$.

Then $P_L$ has a kernel $K_L$ satisfying $\sup_x\int|K_L(x,y)|dy\le C'$ and $K_L(x,y)=0$ when $\operatorname{dist}(x,y)>C'2^{-L}$. If $a$ is $\beta$-Hölder for $0<\beta\le1$, then
$$\|P_L(ah)-ah\|_\infty\le C'\|a\|_{C^\beta}2^{-\beta L}\|h\|_\infty,\qquad h\in V_L.$$
For the composition assertion, assume additionally an integer $m>\alpha$ such that $\|\psi_{lk}^{(q)}\|_\infty\le C_q2^{l(q+1/2)}$ for $0\le q\le m$, bounded overlap also for their derivatives, and vanishing moments through degree $m-1$ for the detail wavelets, including boundary wavelets; the finite low scaling functions are $C^m$. These are the usual sufficiently regular compact wavelet hypotheses. If a bounded function $g$ has coefficients bounded by $C_g2^{-l(\alpha+1/2)}$, with $\alpha>0$, and its wavelet expansion represents $g$ in $L^2$, then $\|g-P_Lg\|_\infty\le C''C_g2^{-\alpha L}$, up to equality of the continuous representatives. Under these additional derivative and cancellation hypotheses, $e^g$ also has coefficients bounded by $C_g^\prime2^{-l(\alpha+1/2)}$, including integer $\alpha$, and $g,e^g$ are $\beta$-Hölder for every $0<\beta<\min(\alpha,1)$. Moreover $\|h\|_\infty\le C''\sqrt{d_L}\|h\|_2$ for $h\in V_L$.

references.title: Castillo and Nickl, On the Bernstein–von Mises phenomenon for nonparametric Bayes procedures, §2 and §5.4

manifest_rows.title: Type-S posterior contracts in quotient log-density coordinates without a tail restriction on a log-Lipschitz prior
manifest_rows.statement:
Assume AC for the imported measure and Gaussian interfaces. Use Type-S priors and either cutoff of [[def-type-s-and-h-multiscale-density-priors]] with the compact multiresolution basis of [[lem-compact-wavelet-projection-kernel-and-commutator]], regular enough for the truth's Hölder approximation. Suppose $0<\rho_0\le f_0\le D_0$, $g_0=\log f_0\in C^\alpha$, and $\alpha>1/2$. In S1 take $\sigma_l=2^{-l(\alpha+1/2)}$ and any probability density whose logarithm is Lipschitz on all of $\mathbb R$. In S2 take Gaussian coefficients with $\sigma_l=2^{-l(r+1/2)}$ and $0<r<\alpha-1/4$.

Write $d=\dim V_{L_n}\asymp2^{L_n}$, $E_{L_n}=V_{L_n}\cap\{h:\int h=0\}$, $\theta=T-\int T$, $\theta_*=P_{L_n}g_0-\int g_0$, and $e_n=\sqrt{d/n}+d^{-\alpha}$. Under IID data of density $f_0$, the posterior distributions of $\|\theta-\theta_*\|_2/e_n$ are tight in probability. Equivalently, for every deterministic $b_n\to\infty$,
$$\Pi(\|\theta-\theta_*\|_2>b_ne_n\mid X^n)\to0$$
in $P_0^n$-probability. The normalizer defining the posterior is positive and finite $P_0^n$-almost surely. The quotient prior has a positive continuous Lebesgue density $q_L$ on $E_L$. In S1 it obeys
$$|\log q_L(\theta+u)-\log q_L(\theta)|\le B_L\|u\|_2,\qquad B_L^2\le C\sum_{l\le L}2^l\sigma_l^{-2},$$
and a shift in a single high wavelet coordinate obeys the sharper bound $C|u_{lk}|/\sigma_l$. The low scaling block has a fixed finite collection of analogous weighted bounds. In S2 the quotient prior is centered Gaussian, with precision $Q_L$ diagonal on high wavelets with entries $\sigma_l^{-2}$ and a fixed positive definite low scaling block. Its log-density increment is $-\langle Q_L\theta,u\rangle-\langle Q_Lu,u\rangle/2$.

references.title: Castillo, On Bayesian supremum norm contraction rates, §3.2.1 and §4.3; preliminary contraction here obtained by a finite-dimensional likelihood argument
Castillo and Nickl, On the Bernstein–von Mises phenomenon for nonparametric Bayes procedures, §3.2

manifest_rows.title: Type-S density posteriors satisfy the weak multiscale Bernstein–von Mises theorem
manifest_rows.statement:
Assume AC. Let $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ be IID on $[0,1]$ with density $0<\rho_0\le f_0\le D_0<\infty$, and suppose $g_0=\log f_0\in C^\alpha$. Use a sufficiently regular compactly supported boundary corrected orthonormal multiresolution wavelet basis satisfying [[lem-compact-wavelet-projection-kernel-and-commutator]], with regularity greater than $\alpha$, and let $V_L$ contain exactly its wavelet levels through $L$, including the fixed low scaling space and constants. Its regularity and vanishing moments satisfy the composition hypotheses in that lemma for some integer $m>\alpha$. Let $L_n$ be either of the two cutoff sequences in [[def-type-s-and-h-multiscale-density-priors]], fixed consistently for all $n$.

In Type-S1 take $\alpha>1$, $\sigma_l=2^{-l(\alpha+1/2)}$, and any coefficient probability density with globally Lipschitz logarithm. In Type-S2 take $\alpha>1/2$, Gaussian coefficients, and $\sigma_l=2^{-l(r+1/2)}$ with $0<r<\alpha-1/4$. Normalize $f=\exp(T)/\int\exp(T)$ as in that definition. For every admissible weight sequence $w$, the posterior satisfies
$$\beta_{BL,M_0(w)}\bigl(\mathcal L(\sqrt n(f-P_n(L_n))\mid X^n),\mathcal L(G_{P_0})\bigr)\longrightarrow0$$
in $P_0^n$-probability, where $P_n(L_n)$ has empirical wavelet coefficients through $L_n$ and zero coefficients above $L_n$, and $G_{P_0}$ is the Borel Gaussian bridge with covariance $P_0[(\psi_i-P_0\psi_i)(\psi_j-P_0\psi_j)]$.

references.title: Castillo and Nickl, On the Bernstein–von Mises phenomenon for nonparametric Bayes procedures, Theorem 3 and §5.4; direct contraction and commutator proof here retains the approved richer prior scope
Castillo, On Bayesian supremum norm contraction rates, §4.3

manifest_rows.title: Type-S log-density and type-H histogram prior families
manifest_rows.statement:
For type S use a fixed sufficiently regular compactly supported orthonormal multiresolution wavelet basis $(\psi_{lk})$ on $[0,1]$ as in [[def-negative-sobolev-space-for-white-noise]], with boundary correction, regularity greater than the truth smoothness $\alpha$, and $|K_l|=2^l$. The spaces $V_L$ spanned by the retained levels $l\le L$ contain constants and have orthonormal scaling bases with uniformly bounded overlap, support diameters at most $C2^{-L}$, and suprema at most $C2^{L/2}$; a fixed shift of the scaling-resolution index is absorbed in $C$. The wavelets likewise have uniformly bounded overlap, support diameters at most $C2^{-l}$, and suprema at most $C2^{l/2}$. For an integer $m>\alpha$, the detail wavelets have vanishing moments through degree $m-1$, and derivatives through order $m$ satisfy $\|\psi_{lk}^{(q)}\|_\infty\le C_q2^{l(q+1/2)}$, with uniformly bounded overlap of their supports; the fixed low scaling functions are $C^m$. These are the sufficiently regular compact multiresolution basis conditions in the source density theorem. For the density-model source results, every truth $f_0$ is a probability density satisfying $0<\rho_0\le f_0\le D_0<\infty$ for constants $\rho_0,D_0$. For $n\ge3$ and smoothness index $\alpha>0$, let $j_n$ and $\ell_n$ be the largest integers satisfying
$$2^{j_n}\le n^{1/(2\alpha+1)},\qquad 2^{\ell_n}\le(n/\log n)^{1/(2\alpha+1)}.$$
Choose one cutoff sequence $L_n\in\{j_n,\ell_n\}$ for all $n\ge3$; set any finite $L_n$ for $n=1,2$, which does not change asymptotic claims.

For a finite wavelet series $T_n=\sum_{l\le L_n}\sum_{k\in K_l}\sigma_l\xi_{lk}\psi_{lk}$, define $c(T_n)=\log\int_0^1e^{T_n(x)}dx$ and the normalized log-density $f_n(x)=e^{T_n(x)-c(T_n)}$.

The **type-S1 family** takes IID coefficients $\xi_{lk}$ with a continuous density $\varphi_H$ for which $\log\varphi_H$ is Lipschitz, and uses $\sigma_l=2^{-l(\alpha+1/2)}$. Its source theorem assumes $\log f_0$ has coefficient Hölder regularity $\alpha>1$ and $f_0$ is bounded above and bounded away from zero.

The **type-S2 family** takes IID standard-normal coefficients and uses $\sigma_l=2^{-l(r+1/2)}$, where $0<r<\alpha-1/4$; its source theorem uses $\log f_0\in C^\alpha$, $\alpha>1/2$, and positive finite density bounds.

For the **type-H family**, use the Haar basis instead of the regular type-S wavelets: its scaling function is $1$ and $\psi_{lk}=2^{l/2}(1_{I_{l+1,2k}}-1_{I_{l+1,2k+1}})$ for $l\ge0$ and $0\le k<2^l$. The histogram space at resolution $L$ consists of the scaling coordinate and detail levels $l<L$; all detail coefficients at $l\ge L$ vanish. Partition $[0,1]$ into dyadic cells $I_{L_n,k}$ of length $2^{-L_n}$, draw $\omega=(\omega_k)_{k<2^{L_n}}\sim\operatorname{Dirichlet}(a_{0,L_n},\ldots,a_{2^{L_n}-1,L_n})$, and set $f_n=2^{L_n}\omega_k$ on cell $I_{L_n,k}$. The source assumptions are $c_1 2^{-L_na}\le a_{k,L_n}\le c_2$ for fixed positive $a,c_1,c_2$, and $f_0\in C^\alpha$ for $1/2<\alpha\le1$, together with the common positive finite density bounds above. The posterior asymptotic conclusions for these families are separate results.

Here $C^\alpha_\psi$ denotes the coefficient class with norm $\|g\|_{C^\alpha_\psi}:=\sup_{l,k}2^{l(\alpha+1/2)}|\langle g,\psi_{lk}\rangle|$. For sufficiently regular standard wavelets this is the usual Hölder scale (with the usual Zygmund interpretation at integer smoothness).

references.title: Castillo and Nickl, On the Bernstein–von Mises phenomenon for nonparametric Bayes procedures, §§2–3.2, equations (19)–(25)
Giné and Nickl, Mathematical Foundations of Infinite-Dimensional Statistical Models, §7.4 Notes

manifest_rows.title: Little-o multiscale coefficient space M0(w)
manifest_rows.statement:
Use the wavelet coefficient levels $(l,k)$ and multiplicities $|K_l|=2^l$ from [[def-negative-sobolev-space-for-white-noise]]. The same coefficient-space definition applies to the Haar system used for type-H histograms: detail levels $l\ge0$ have $2^l$ coefficients, and the single scaling coefficient is an additional finite coarsest coordinate, included in the norm with weight $1$. Finite projections always retain that scaling coordinate; this finite convention does not alter any tail assertion. Let $w=(w_l)$ be nondecreasing with $w_l\ge1$. Define
$$M(w)=\left\{x=(x_{lk}):\|x\|_{M(w)}:=\sup_l\frac{\max_{k\in K_l}|x_{lk}|}{w_l}<\infty\right\}$$
and its closed little-o subspace
$$M_0(w)=\left\{x\in M(w):\frac{\max_{k\in K_l}|x_{lk}|}{w_l}\longrightarrow0\text{ as }l\to\infty\right\},$$
with the same norm. Call $w$ admissible when $w_l/\sqrt l\to\infty$. The finite coarsest level is included in the norm and does not affect this limit. Elements are coefficient sequences; in particular, they need not be $L^2$ functions. [[lem-m0w-separable-and-projection-tails]] proves that $M_0(w)$ is a separable Banach space, that $L^2$ coefficient sequences embed in it, and that finite-level projections converge in its norm.

references.title: Castillo and Nickl, On the Bernstein–von Mises phenomenon for nonparametric Bayes procedures, §2.1, equations (11)–(12)
Giné and Nickl, Mathematical Foundations of Infinite-Dimensional Statistical Models, §5.2.2 and §7.3.4

manifest_rows.title: The multiscale primitive map is continuous into C[0,1]
manifest_rows.statement:
Let $(\psi_{lk})$ be a compactly supported wavelet basis of [[def-negative-sobolev-space-for-white-noise]]. The Haar basis with its finite scaling coordinate, as specified in [[def-multiscale-coefficient-space-m0w]], is also allowed. Assume each level-$l$ wavelet for $l\ge l_0$ has zero integral, uniformly bounded overlap, support length at most $C_0 2^{-l}$, and $\|\psi_{lk}\|_1\le C_0 2^{-l/2}$. Let $M_0(w)$ be as in [[def-multiscale-coefficient-space-m0w]], and suppose
$$S_w:=\sum_{l\ge l_0}w_l2^{-l/2}<\infty.$$
For $x\in M_0(w)$ define
$$Jx(t):=\sum_{l,k}x_{lk}\langle 1_{[0,t]},\psi_{lk}\rangle_{L^2},\qquad 0\le t\le1.$$
Then this series converges absolutely and uniformly in $t$, $Jx\in C([0,1])$, and $\|Jx-Jy\|_\infty\le C S_w\|x-y\|_{M(w)}$ after adding the finite coarsest-level constant to $C S_w$. If $x$ is the coefficient sequence of $f\in L^2$, then $Jx(t)=\int_0^t f(u)\,du$.

references.title: Castillo and Nickl, On the Bernstein–von Mises phenomenon for nonparametric Bayes procedures, §4.1
Giné and Nickl, Mathematical Foundations of Infinite-Dimensional Statistical Models, proof of Theorem 7.3.20

manifest_rows.title: Uniform truth under type-S and type-H density priors
manifest_rows.statement: The uniform truth $f_0=1$ meets the truth-side smoothness and positive-bound conditions for both a type-S log-density prior and a type-H dyadic histogram prior. The weight sequence $w_l=\max(1,\sqrt l\log(l+1))$ is admissible and also satisfies the extra summability needed for the CDF map. Thus the source-specific posterior BvM and credible-band conclusions of [[cor-type-s-h-density-credible-band-calibration]] apply to these choices.

references.title: Castillo and Nickl, On the Bernstein–von Mises phenomenon for nonparametric Bayes procedures, §3.2

manifest_rows.title: Type-S and Type-H density credible bands have asymptotically exact coverage
manifest_rows.statement:
Assume AC. Use either Type-S1, Type-S2 or Type-H with all the truth, basis, prior-scale, Dirichlet-parameter and cutoff conditions of [[def-type-s-and-h-multiscale-density-priors]]. Let $w_l\ge1$ be nondecreasing, $w_l/\sqrt{l+1}\to\infty$, and $\sum_lw_l2^{-l/2}<\infty$. In Type S take $T_n=P_n(L_n)$, the empirical wavelet projection through level $L_n$. In Type H take the empirical histogram $T_n=h_n$ at mesh $2^{-L_n}$, equivalently the Haar projection with scaling coordinate and details $l<L_n$.

For each $0<\eta<1$, the posterior multiscale and CDF balls of [[thm-cdf-and-multiscale-credible-band-calibration-from-bvm]], at posterior level $1-\eta$ and centered at these $T_n$, have posterior mass at least $1-\eta$ and frequentist coverage tending to $1-\eta$. Their scaled radii converge in probability to the positive finite $1-\eta$ quantiles of the corresponding Gaussian bridge norms. In particular the CDF posterior converges in bounded-Lipschitz distance to the $P_0$-Brownian bridge law.

If additionally the coefficient smoothness and undersmoothing hypotheses of [[thm-multiscale-credible-band-holder-diameter]] hold, its intersection with the stated coefficient smoothness ball has the same limiting coverage and the diameter bound asserted there. No unverified entropy, prior-mass, posterior contraction or quantile-regularity premise is required in this corollary.

references.title: Castillo and Nickl, On the Bernstein–von Mises phenomenon for nonparametric Bayes procedures, Theorems 3–5

page_proposals.current_body_exact:
## Objective

This page develops scalar functional BvM limits and credible-interval calibration in Gaussian white noise, including the nonlinear delta-method condition. It defines the multiscale coefficient space and the type-S and type-H density prior interfaces, then proves the source-specific density weak BvM theorems and their CDF and multiscale credible-band consequences, with the required sampling-process and Gaussian norm-quantile limits. It records the exact smoothness, positivity, topology, centering, and rate assumptions used in each result.

For type S, local quotient-likelihood contraction, wavelet composition and projection estimates, and posterior Laplace bounds prove the weak BvM under both approved coefficient-prior regimes. For type H, the Dirichlet posterior and normalized-Gamma concentration give a direct conjugate proof. The resulting empirical-center credible bands have asymptotically exact coverage; the stated additional coefficient smoothness and undersmoothing assumptions give the diameter bound.

page_proposals.current_body_exact: This page proves the product-prior weak Bernstein–von Mises limit in the Gaussian white-noise model. Countable choice supplies the $L^2$ completeness used for the prior and suffices for the scalar density-normal interface; the posterior kernel is a supplied model object, and the projection/tail proof uses no further choice axiom.
